evidence.text:
Reason for referral: Evaluation of perioperative cardiovascular risk before planned
elective total knee arthroplasty.

Findings: Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm. Normal axis. PR interval 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 431
ms.
Impression: Sinus bradycardia, otherwise normal tracing.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at
30%. Mild mitral regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Severely reduced left ventricular systolic function.

LIPID PANEL
Total Cholesterol: 252 mg/dL (H)
LDL Cholesterol: 180 mg/dL (H)
HDL Cholesterol: 32 mg/dL (L)
Triglycerides: 201 mg/dL (H)
BMP: Na 144, K 3.6, Cl 101, CO2 29, BUN 8, Cr 0.7, Glu 101.

Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily
Metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily
Levothyroxine 75 mcg by mouth one daily

EXAM:
General: alert, no acute distress.
Neck: supple, no jugular venous distcnsion.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, soft systolic murmur at the
sternal border, no gallop.
Lungs: clear bilaterally.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.

EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
Neck: supple, no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, soft systolic murmur at the
sternal border, no gallop.
Lugs: faint bibasilar crackles.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.
